messages:
paul: Quick check — thinking about reshaping queue topology to support tenant re-sharding for hotspots. Idea: move from strict per-tenant lanes to a hybrid sharding model where tiny tenants share dynamic slots and heavy hitters get pinned shards. Main worries: KV cache affinity, preemption semantics, and headroom accounting. Anyone see fatal flaws?
anya: Nice. Main risk is KV cache churn if we reshuffle frequently. We need cache-aware moves (don't evict hot keys).
jin: Agree. Soft-reshard (weight hints + gradual cutover) can keep most of the KV warm. Rollout timing is crucial — we should guard with telemetry thresholds.
maya: Sketch of a config for trials:
```
shard_policy: "hybrid"
large_threshold_tokens: 1000000
reshard_window_sec: 3600
move_batch_size: 5
preserve_kv_ttl_sec: 300
```
Also plan to emit `reshard_reason` and `reshard_start/end` events.
paul: Good point. How do we handle tail latency while moving shards? Options: preemptive drain vs instant cutover.
anya: Prefer drain+canary. Mark destination shard as receiving, start redirecting new enqueues, drain inflight. Adds complexity to lease semantics though.
jin: We can reuse lease-heartbeat plumbing and add `reshard_grace` + `kv_pin` flags on leases. Experiment in staging first with synthetic traffic.
maya: Telemetry we need: token-per-shard, kv-miss-rate, p99 latency per-tenant, eviction-rate, move-duration. Add rolling counters and a prometheus label `reshard_id`.
paul: Admission implications: during reshuffle we may temporarily double-enqueue for tenants. Admission should avoid dropping already-queued requests.
anya: Admission policy idea: favor older enqueues (preserve FIFO). New requests during move get routed to fallback model/replica or get `retry-after`. Also a short `admission_hold` flag while migrating.
jin: Edge case: long-running streaming responses — we must keep slot/kv pinned until stream finishes or cost of migrating state is paid. Migration mid-stream is messy.
maya: Proposal: do NOT migrate active KV. Keep the old shard serving active streams until idle TTL expires, then mark it removable. Much cheaper than sync.
paul: That implies temporary duplication of KV state and some extra GPU memory. Acceptable?
anya: I think so for short windows. Need SLO guardrails to abort moves if duplication exceeds threshold. :warning:
jin: I'll draft an experiment plan: AB test on a slice of noisy tenants, measure p50/p95/p99, cache miss delta, GPU utilization, and eviction delta.
maya: I'll add config toggles and rollout gates in Console: per-customer flag `allow_reshard`, global `reshard_enabled`, and visibility for in-flight moves.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy queued for `shard_manager:v2` to staging cluster. Logs at: https://deploys/internal/6912345678 — will publish canary results when done.
paul: Thanks. I'll draft RFC that includes 3 strategies: (1) sticky-pinned for big tenants, (2) soft-reshard with drain, (3) immediate-cutover (emergency only). Action items: Jin — experiment plan; Maya — config + telemetry; Anya — refine admission contract + SLO aborts.
anya: On it. Also pinging @ops-team for any backup/KMS implications from temporary KV duplication.
paul: OK — aim to have RFC + proto config + staging run by EOD Friday. Short, focused experiment. :thumbsup:
